observations: The source text of LM2 Torah 59 is a short, structurally unified teaching built around a single paradox: 'זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר, זָרִיז וְנִפְסָד' (the zealous one gains; the zealous one loses). The Rebbe resolves this paradox by distinguishing two types of spiritual path: (1) the tzaddik who goes מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא (from level to level) — for whom there exists a precious 'בְּחִינָה שֶׁבֵּין הַמִּצְווֹת' (dimension between the mitzvot) that rushing causes him to skip over, so rushing makes him lose (זָרִיז וְנִפְסָד); (2) the ba'al teshuva who has no such gradual in-between dimension and must leap directly to holiness, so rushing is correct and he gains (זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר). The text explicitly illustrates the 'in-between dimension' as the preamble phrases in the Torah before a mitzvah is stated (e.g., 'וַיְדַבֵּר ה' אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ'), teaching that even those introductory words contain divine service. To qualify for a new package, there must be 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina equating language ('X הוּא בְּחִינַת Y') forming an independent domain. This condition is not met: the text uses 'בְּחִינָה' throughout as a noun ('a dimension,' 'a level') rather than as the symmetric equivalence formula that would create concept-to-concept bechina links. The teaching is entirely causal in structure — a chain of conditional if/then reasoning about timing and path-type — which maps to eitza logic. The two dataset entries for reference 1059 ('cause' and 'eitza' types) correctly capture the only formalizable relationship in this text: the directional link between מצוה and בין המצוות. No new packages are warranted.
